source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with pleurisy has sharp pain on breathing. Which position helps splint the chest?
questions.rationale: Turning onto the affected side splints the chest wall and reduces pleural stretch.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Pleurisy Interventions (PDF p. 333)
questions.quote: Instruct the patient to turn onto the affected side to splint the chest wall

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Accumulation of pus in the pleural space is called:
questions.rationale: Empyema is purulent pleural fluid, often after pneumonia or lung abscess.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Empyema (PDF p. 333)
questions.quote: Accumulation of purulent fluid in the pleural space

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Pneumonia developing 4 days after hospital admission is classified as:
questions.rationale: Hospital-acquired pneumonia begins more than 48 hours after admission.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Pneumonia (PDF p. 333)
questions.quote: onset of pneumonia symptoms more than 48 hours after admission

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Rusty sputum, sudden high fever, and pleuritic pain suggest:
questions.rationale: Bacterial pneumonia: abrupt fever, purulent or rusty sputum, pleuritic pain.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Pneumonia (PDF p. 333)
questions.quote: Rusty, blood-tinged sputum

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: How much daily fluid helps liquefy secretions in pneumonia, unless contraindicated?
questions.rationale: Hydration of 2–3 L/day liquefies secretions.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Pneumonia Interventions (PDF p. 333)
questions.quote: Promote hydration (2-3 L/day) to liquefy secretions

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client on antibiotics for pneumonia feels better on day 3. The nurse teaches:
questions.rationale: Finish the entire 7–10 day course; improvement is expected within 48–72 hours.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Pneumonia Teaching (PDF p. 334)
questions.quote: Teach the need to continue entire course of antimicrobial therapy

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which test confirms active pulmonary tuberculosis?
questions.rationale: Sputum smear and culture confirm TB; PPD shows infection; x-ray shows extent.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Pulmonary Tuberculosis (PDF p. 334)
questions.quote: Sputum smear/Sputum culture confirms a diagnosis of TB

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Why is pyridoxine (vitamin B6) given with isoniazid?
questions.rationale: Pyridoxine prevents INH-associated peripheral neuritis.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, TB Management (PDF p. 334)
questions.quote: Vitamin B (pyridoxine) is usually administered with INH

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which anti-TB drug requires periodic visual acuity and color vision tests?
questions.rationale: Ethambutol can cause optic neuritis.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Anti-TB Drugs (PDF p. 335)
questions.quote: Optic neuritis (may lead to blindness

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A client on pyrazinamide reports joint pain. The nurse suspects:
questions.rationale: Pyrazinamide causes hyperuricemia, arthralgia, and hepatotoxicity.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Anti-TB Drugs (PDF p. 334)
questions.quote: Hyperuricemia, hepatotoxicity, skin rash, arthralgias

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: When should anti-TB drugs be taken for best absorption?
questions.rationale: Take on an empty stomach or at least 1 hour before meals; food interferes with absorption.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, TB Nursing Interventions (PDF p. 335)
questions.quote: take the medication either on an empty stomach or at least 1 hour before meals

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A client on INH should avoid which food to prevent flushing and palpitations?
questions.rationale: INH users should avoid tyramine and histamine foods (aged cheese, tuna, skipjack).
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, TB Nursing Interventions (PDF p. 335)
questions.quote: Patients taking INH should avoid foods that contain tyramine and histamine

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: The hallmark of ARDS is hypoxemia that:
options: Does not respond to supplemental oxygen
questions.rationale: Refractory hypoxemia with bilateral infiltrates and reduced compliance characterize ARDS.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, ARDS (PDF p. 335)
questions.quote: Arterial hypoxemia that does not respond to supplemental oxygen

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which ventilator setting usually improves oxygenation in ARDS?
questions.rationale: PEEP keeps alveoli open and usually improves oxygenation.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, ARDS Management (PDF p. 335)
questions.quote: PEEP usually improves oxygenation

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client 3 days after hip surgery suddenly has dyspnea, pleuritic chest pain, and tachypnea. The nurse suspects:
questions.rationale: Sudden dyspnea and tachypnea after orthopedic surgery suggest PE.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Pulmonary Embolism (PDF p. 336)
questions.quote: Dyspnea is the most frequent symptom

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: The nurse suspects pulmonary embolism. What is the first action?
questions.rationale: Nasal oxygen is given immediately to relieve hypoxemia.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, PE Management (PDF p. 336)
questions.quote: Nasal oxygen is administered immediately to relieve hypoxemia

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which test is considered the best method to diagnose pulmonary embolism?
questions.rationale: Pulmonary angiography is the best method; V/Q scan and spiral CT are also used.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, PE Diagnostics (PDF p. 336)
questions.quote: Pulmonary angiography is considered the best method to diagnose PE

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: ABG findings in acute pulmonary embolism typically show:
questions.rationale: Hypoxemia with low PaCO2 from hyperventilation.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, PE Diagnostics (PDF p. 336)
questions.quote: Arterial blood gas analysis – shows hypoxemia and hypocapnia

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which substance secreted by the stomach is needed to absorb vitamin B12?
questions.rationale: Intrinsic factor from the gastric mucosa combines with dietary B12.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Gastric Function (PDF p. 337)
questions.quote: Secreted by the gastric mucosa, combines w/ dietary vitamin B12

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which enzyme begins starch digestion in the mouth?
questions.rationale: Salivary amylase starts starch digestion.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Chewing and Swallowing (PDF p. 337)
questions.quote: Is an enzyme that begins the digestion of starches

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: What is the primary function of the colon?
questions.rationale: Slow peristalsis allows water and electrolyte reabsorption.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Colonic Function (PDF p. 338)
questions.quote: efficient reabsorption of water and electrolytes, which is the primary purpose of the colon

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: During abdominal assessment, which technique is performed right after inspection?
questions.rationale: Order: inspection, auscultation, percussion, palpation, to avoid altering bowel sounds.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, GI Physical Examination (PDF p. 338)
questions.quote: Auscultation

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: The appendix is located in which abdominal region?
questions.rationale: Right inguinal contains the cecum, appendix, and lower ileum.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Abdominal Regions (PDF p. 339)
questions.quote: Appendix

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Before an upper GI series, the nurse advises the client to avoid:
questions.rationale: Smoking, gum, and mints stimulate gastric motility; client is NPO from midnight.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Upper GI Series (PDF p. 339)
questions.quote: Smoking, chewing gum, and mints can stimulate gastric motility

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: After a barium enema, the nurse should instruct the client to:
questions.rationale: Increase fluids and give laxative to evacuate barium; monitor bowel movements.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Lower GI Series (PDF p. 339)
questions.quote: Increased fluid intake after the procedure.
